# Repository fixtures

Repositories are generated in pytest temporary directories rather than checked in as
nested Git repositories. `tests/conftest.py` provides the `git` helper and `git_repo`
fixture. No external repositories or credentials are used.

| Case | Generator / tests | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| basic-context | `git_repo`; `test_basic_context_repository`; rendering/CLI tests | Instructions, architecture, stable manifest, unborn Git HEAD |
| history | `test_history_repository_inventory`; classification table | Historical architecture/ADR overlay, unknown generic document |
| git-ignore | `test_git_ignore_dirty_and_raw_bytes` | Tracked sources, ignored and untracked files, ordinary code exclusion |
| dirty | Same test; worktree/rename test | Clean HEAD compared to modified raw bytes; staged rename |
| warnings | Acquisition safety tests; CLI warning test | Symlinks, size limit/growth, unreadability, hash/metadata failures |

The checked-in `tests/fixtures/inventory-v1*.json` manifests cover basic-context, dirty,
and historical repositories.
Its remote identity is fixed, branches/commit metadata and file bytes are fixed, so it contains
no temporary paths or observation timestamps. Update it only for an intentional schema/output change
and inspect the resulting contract. Fixtures contain synthetic text only.


Phase 1 fixtures are generated by `authority_repo` in `tests/test_authority.py`: ten tiny
synthetic documents covering instructions, ADRs, architecture/product, plans, verification,
current-state, historical content, and unknown authority. `CONFIG` adds a whole-policy
replacement, custom policy, class override, template exclusion, historical override, and
stale metadata warning. The three `tests/fixtures/authority-v1-*.json` goldens cover
architectural intent, missing executable truth, and config-driven resolution. To regenerate,
run the corresponding `test_authority_golden` construction and write its rendered result to
the matching fixture; inspect changes before accepting them. Repository/source identities
are fixed in that test to isolate projection semantics from temporary paths.

`tests/test_configuration.py` generates invalid configs and controlled read/replacement races
at test time. No large repositories, downloaded content, or source bodies are stored in the
authority JSON fixtures.

Phase 2 fixtures are generated by `lifecycle_repo`, `scenario_config`, and `fixed_manifest`
in `tests/test_lifecycle.py`. Three small lifecycle JSON goldens cover explicit states,
a three-ADR chain, and historical override with a missing endpoint. The separate
`authority-v1-lifecycle.json` adds lifecycle-aware resolution without changing Phase 1
fixtures. The chain repeats endpoint projections deliberately to pin direct relation
identities/revisions; it contains only four tiny documents plus config. To regenerate,
construct each scenario in a temporary directory, apply `fixed_manifest`, render with
`render_lifecycle_json(lifecycle_overview(manifest))`, and write the matching fixture.
For the chain authority golden, render `resolve_authority` for `architectural_intent`.
Inspect the resulting explicit contracts before accepting changes. State/graph/security
matrices generate their remaining inputs at test time; no large source fixtures are stored.
